system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Advising:** Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer)
**Reviewed:** Seller's covering positions note and Disclosure Letter, both treated as untrusted counterparty material

---

## Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced". On almost every risk allocation point it departs from our playbook. Three patterns run through it:

1. **Fallback numbers are presented as starting positions.** The 20% cap and the 18-month period both match our fallbacks. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost to use either for this draft, so neither is cleared.
2. **Catch-all drafting would quietly collapse our separate regimes.** The "applies to all Claims" wording in clauses 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5, the "settled under the general regime" statement on Tax/IP, and the proposal to fold title into the general caps would together bring fraud, title, tax, IP and the indemnities under the general limitations.
3. **The covering note contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** It calls Bluefen "addressed" and DD-006 "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter says no Bluefen consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists, and that the incident's scope, access and notification position are undetermined. We should rely on the disclosed facts, not the characterisations.

---

## 1. Limitation regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller proposes 20% (AUD 4.8m). Reject.
- **Our position:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback. Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3, a matching number does not clear it. It needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Action:** Hold 25%. Do not signal flexibility. If the team wants to move, seek Amelia's written authority first, referencing this Seller Update draft.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): Seller proposes AUD 25k de minimis and an AUD 250k basket, recoverable only above the basket. Reject.
- **Our position:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- Combined effect of the Seller's terms: the de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and switching from a tipping basket to a deductible strips the first AUD 250k out of every recovery. With a reduced cap on top, this materially hollows out the warranty package.
- **Action:** Restore 5k / 50k / first-dollar tipping basket.
- Also confirm in drafting that de minimis claims of the same or related nature are aggregated. Otherwise the Seller could argue that each instance of a recurring issue falls below the de minimis.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3/13): Seller proposes 18 months, plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". Reject both.
- **Our position:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The "applies to all Claims" sentence is the more dangerous element. It is a hidden general-regime override. It reverses the default, so every Claim (Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant and payment claims, fraud) is capped, basketed and time-barred unless we successfully carve each one out. Any drafting gap would then fall in the Seller's favour.
- **Action:** Delete it. Reverse the default: the clause 12 limitations apply only to "General Warranty Claims" as defined. Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories expressly separate.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title / Capacity: Seller proposes the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity". Reject.
- **Our position:** a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap the Seller's liability for not owning what it is selling at 20% of the price. Title and capacity go to the heart of the bargain.
- **Action:** Restore the fundamental regime in full.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) "apply to all Claims of any nature". Reject.
- As drafted, this would extend caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**.
- **Our position is non-negotiable:** these are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one, including the deal team, may waive this.
- **Action:** Insert an express overriding carve-out. Also exclude the specific indemnities and the Title/Tax/IP regimes from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.

### 1.6 Tax and IP: Seller treats them as "settled under the general regime". Reject the characterisation.
- Per the playbook, Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Nothing has been agreed.
- We should be equally careful in the other direction. We have not secured unlimited liability or any other resolution, and our mark-up should not imply that we have.
- **Action:** State in the cover note to our mark-up that Tax and IP remain open and are not subject to the general regime. Do not let "settled" go unanswered, or it will later be cited as agreed.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7). Reject.
- The Seller discloses everything in the data room as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Our position:** specific fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Action:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosures should qualify only the warranties they are made against, and only to the extent fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
- Specify that disclosure **never** qualifies the Title/Capacity warranties or any specific indemnity. The Disclosure Letter's own specific items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) are precisely the matters our indemnities and conditions are designed to address.
- **Cl 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in principle, but add that it does not limit the Seller's liability under any indemnity, condition or covenant.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). Reject.
- The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records. This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion combined with constructive knowledge. Read with 2.1, it effectively turns due diligence into a waiver.
- **Our position:** delete it entirely. If a knowledge concept survives, it should be a **Seller** knowledge qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and Completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3). Reject. The covering note is inconsistent with the Disclosure Letter.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter item 2 / DD-002):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. Its change-control clause 11.2 has conditions in 11.3. The Seller has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller's proposal:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. That does not "address" the issue. It means we could be required to complete holding a consent whose conditions are unmet, and lose our largest customer.
- **Our position:** a condition precedent requiring an effective consent **and** evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. No consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this materiality.
- **Action:** Redraft the CP. Make it waivable only by the Buyer. Add a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7). Reject the post-Completion release.
- **Facts (item 3 / DD-003):** about AUD 3.2m outstanding (the figure is approximate). Change-control is at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been provided.
- The deal is **debt-free/cash-free**. A release "to be provided following Completion" leaves the Company, and potentially the shares (see Title below), encumbered after we have paid.
- **Our position:** a current payout letter, with repayment made **directly from Completion funds** to Riverlark, and effective releases of security (deeds of release and PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- Any post-Completion release would need both an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is offered.
- **Action:** Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, so the approximate AUD 3.2m is replaced with a verified figure including interest and break costs. Route the payout through the funds flow and make release documents a Completion deliverable.

### 3.3 Employee completion bonuses: funds flow (DD-005). Reject the silent exclusion.
- **Facts (item 5):** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, which do **not** appear in the draft funds flow. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) are not addressed.
- Calling these "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. The bonuses are Company obligations to Company employees. If not dealt with, the cost falls on the Buyer after Completion, even though the price is debt-free/cash-free.
- **Our position:** treat the AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** either as a specific line item deducted in the funds flow, or as Seller-funded with an indemnity.
- **Action:** Request a schedule of recipients, amounts, conditions and the payroll tax and super treatment. We should not invent an on-cost number; ask the Seller to quantify it. Also cover bonuses that become payable after Completion on continued-employment conditions.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010). Reject "adequate". Broaden the indemnity.
- **Facts (item 4):** under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open. The Seller itself notes this is not independent bank verification. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the debt but not the real exposure: the Company may not own IP it uses.
- **Our position:** broaden the indemnity to all Losses arising from any Ironquay claim regarding ownership, use or infringement of Project Materials or related IP, or from any failure to vest that IP in the Company. Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- **Caution:** the AUD 180,000 is unverified in both directions. We should not assert it is unpaid, nor accept that it is paid. Request bank evidence and a statement from Ironquay.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident (DD-006). Reject the "not expected to be material" characterisation. Do not overstate it either.
- **Facts (item 6):** a download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026, it is not established whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- The Seller's own letter does not support a conclusion that the incident is immaterial. Equally, we must **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Action:** Add covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation diligently, with appropriate forensic support;
  - give the Buyer prompt written updates and access to findings;
  - consult the Buyer before any notification decision or regulator or third-party communication.
- Add a specific warranty or indemnity for this incident sitting outside the general cap and basket, and not qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge. Note that the facts are now six weeks old (see section 6).

### 4.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000). Neither accept nor reclassify yet.
- The Seller says these are "ordinary-course operating costs". Its Disclosure Letter (item 8) says the material does **not** state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. It also says they should be read together for timing and scope, since three AUD 110k renewals may in substance be one commitment.
- **Our position:** assess them. There is no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and equally no acceptance of the "ordinary course" label.
- **Action:** Request the contracts, term and termination rights, accrual treatment, approval history and business rationale. Decide on treatment (working capital, Debt, specific indemnity, or ordinary course) once we have the facts.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012). Insufficient evidence.
- The share register is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Action:** Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption and transfer restrictions);
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that no Riverlark or other security extends over the shares (link to 3.2);
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
- Title warranties sit in the fundamental regime (1.4), unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.

### 4.5 Lower-priority items: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's letter says the lease needs a notification only, and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's readings, not established facts.
- **Action:** Have our team review the change-of-control and assignment wording directly. Make the lease notification a Completion or post-Completion deliverable, and confirm that Mossvale has no change-of-control trigger.

---

## 5. Points to resist on process

- Do not treat "agreed price mechanics", "addressed", "adequate", "settled" or "not expected to be material" as agreed or verified. Each is a Seller assertion, and in several cases the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts it.
- Do not agree to any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) without written authority from Amelia Frost specific to this draft.
- The fraud carve-out cannot be traded under any authority.

## 6. Refresh the facts

The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Before finalising the mark-up, request updates on:
- Bluefen consent status;
- the Riverlark payout figure;
- Ironquay payment evidence;
- DD-006 investigation progress;
- Sandbar commitments;
- the bonus schedule and on-costs.

Distinguish verified updates (documents, third-party confirmations) from Seller assertions.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **Hold 25% / 6.0m.** The fallback is not authorised. |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **5k / 50k, first-dollar tipping basket** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** The fallback is not authorised. |
| 4 | "Limits apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete.** Limits apply only to General Warranty Claims. |
| 5 | Title/Capacity | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket and knowledge** |
| 6 | Limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | All Claims incl. fraud | **Full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out (non-waivable)** |
| 7 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Remain OPEN.** Say so expressly. |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Never qualifies title or indemnities. |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. discoverable | **Delete.** Any qualifier is Seller knowledge with named persons and reasonable enquiry. |
| 10 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, before Completion** |
| 11 | Riverlark (~3.2m) | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion** |
| 12 | Bonuses (420k + on-costs) | Excluded from funds flow | **Specific line item or Seller-funded, including all on-costs** |
| 13 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity "adequate" | **Broaden to all Ironquay IP losses. Keep the SOW3 cure. 180k unverified.** |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation and update covenants plus specific protection. No assumed breach or number.** |
| 15 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess. No automatic Debt or price deduction.** Request contracts. |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution, authority** |
| 17 | Facts | As at 22 Sept 2026 | **Refresh all key items. Separate verified updates from assertions.** |

**Next steps:**
1. Prepare a mark-up reinstating playbook starting positions across clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 and Schedule 7, with a Disclosure Letter rider deleting 1.1 and 1.2.
2. Send the Seller an information request covering the items in section 6 and 4.3/4.4.
3. Raise with Amelia Frost only if the team wants authority to use any fallback. Until then, none is in play.
=== END ADVICE ===
